## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

The *Sappaccayaduka* (Patthana 8.7) is a treatise in the *Paṭṭhāna*, the final book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The title designates the dyad (*duka*) of the conditioned, which originates as one of the pairs in the Abhidhamma matrix (*mātikā*), specifically under the *Cūḷantaraduka* (the shorter group of miscellaneous dyads) [Tan 2015]. The dyad analyzes phenomena divided between states that are due to causes or conditions (*sappaccayā dhammā*) and those that are not due to causes (*appaccayā dhammā*) [Tan 2015]. In the *Paṭṭhāna*, these categorical terms are systematically investigated according to the conditional relations (*paccaya*) that govern mental and material phenomena.

No direct external parallels in Chinese, Tibetan, or Sanskrit corpora have been identified for this specific text [DharmaNexus]. However, DharmaNexus identifies widespread internal text reuse across the *Paṭṭhāna*, recording 88 matching passages shared across 19 other *Paṭṭhāna* sections [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial structural and formulaic overlaps occur with *Cūḷantaraduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.3), *Kusalattika, Tika* (Patthana 5.1), *Tika Saraṇaduka* (Patthana 4.8), and *Tika Kusalattika* (Patthana 5.2), along with a verbatim correspondence in *Sappaccayadukādi* (Patthana 14.7) [DharmaNexus].
